titulo: Neighbor protocols as a map: A2A, ACP, AP2, NLWeb, llms.txt — what is still a draft
lead: Every week a new acronym shows up promising to make your site "AI-ready." Almost all of them are drafts or proposals, and each one lives in a different layer. In this lesson you place each neighbor protocol on the map, with a status and a date, and decide for your site: adopt, wait, or does not apply.
objetivo: place each neighbor protocol in the right layer with a dated status, and decide adopt, wait, or does not apply, with a reason.

aprende.t: Which layer each acronym lives in
Proposal, draft, project, and stable, with a date
Adopt, wait, or does not apply, with a reason
The reasons that don't count (ranking, "it will become a standard")

hero_alt: A dark paper map with pins and threads connecting points, next to a row of connectors for different cables.

secoes.sub: Status read from the sources on 10/19/2026. Click each layer.

nos.detalhe: Proposal from 2024-09-03, modified on 2026-08-10. No measured effect on citations; reported by SE Ranking (~10% adoption, no correlation with citations), not confirmed on 10/19/2026. Decision: inemaSEO Track.
CG draft from 10/16/2026; origin trial in Chrome 149–156. Courses 2 and 5.
Revision 2026-07-28, the current one. The only stable one on the map. Course 1.
Open project from Microsoft: each instance is also an MCP server with the ask method and answers in Schema.org. No public adoption count.
One agent talks to another agent. A Linux Foundation project; more than 150 organizations as of 04/09/2026. It only makes sense if your site has an agent of its own.
ACP (OpenAI + Stripe): ChatGPT was the first platform. AP2 (Google, 09/16/2025): version 0.2; donation to the FIDO Alliance reported by the press, not confirmed on 10/19/2026.
Is the visitor who they say they are? draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 (Sep/2026), not an RFC yet. Owner: course 4.

secoes.legenda: None of these is a ranking factor. Citation in AIs is a topic for the inemaSEO Track.

secoes.sub: The label tells you how much you can bet on it.

texto: Someone published the format; nobody has committed to reading it.
E.g., llms.txt. It costs little, but don't promise any effect.
A group document (CG, IETF) still in progress. The API has already changed once (navigator → document).
It has an implementation and an organization behind it (Linux Foundation, a company).
It is not stable: check the version on the day you adopt it.
A published, versioned revision, with a announced change (MCP 2026-07-28).
Even so, pin the SDK version and run the battery when it goes up.

exemplo.texto: Adopting something that is not stable requires revisar_em (a date) and fallback.

secoes.titulo: The decisions for the example site
secoes.sub: One decision per protocol on the map, with a reason. Adopting something that is a draft takes a review date and a fallback.

secoes.titulo: Check the decisions against the map
secoes.sub: vizinhos.mjs reads the dated map (vizinhos/mapa.json, with the source of each row) and your decisions file.

Free workshops: ACP and AP2 do not apply. Web Bot Auth waits for course 4.

PROBLEMA WebMCP: motivo promete ranking ou padrão ("vai ser o padrão da web")
PROBLEMA WebMCP: adotar algo em rascunho pede revisar_em (AAAA-MM-DD) e fallback
PROBLEMA llms.txt: motivo promete ranking ou padrão ("sobe o site no ranking das IAs")
PROBLEMA Web Bot Auth: sem decisão
VIZINHOS: 8 protocolos · 7 decisões · 4 problema(s)
saída: 1

"It will be the standard of the web" and "it moves the site up in the AI rankings" are not reasons: nothing on the map says that. Adopting WebMCP without a review date and without a fallback also fails.

secoes.sub: The file vizinhos/ruim.json has four common problems.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after the answer.

perguntas.p: Which protocol on the map was stable on 10/19/2026?
opcoes: WebMCP, with an origin trial in Chrome 149–156.
Web Bot Auth, published as a draft at the IETF.
perguntas.explica: MCP has a published, versioned revision. WebMCP and Web Bot Auth are drafts; llms.txt is a proposal.

perguntas.p: The site's workshops are free. What should you do with ACP and AP2?
opcoes: Adopt both now, so the site is ready when sales begin.
Mark as not applicable: no payment goes through the site.
Wait for AP2 to become an RFC and adopt only that.
Publish an llms.txt in place of the two.
perguntas.explica: These are purchase and payment layers. With no purchases on the site, they don't apply; if you ever start selling, the decision comes back with that day's date.

perguntas.p: Why does "it raises the site in AI rankings" fail as a reason to adopt llms.txt?
opcoes: Because there is no measured effect; citation in AIs is a topic for inemaSEO.
Because llms.txt only works on sites with WebMCP enabled.
Because the script doesn't accept a reason with more than five words in a row.
Because llms.txt was removed from the proposal in 2026.
perguntas.explica: The proposal exists (modified on 2026-08-10), but there is no measured effect on citation. Promising ranking is exactly what the WebMCP Track avoids.

perguntas.p: You are going to adopt WebMCP on your site. What does the script require besides the reason?
opcoes: The version number of the stable Chrome that ships the API.
An A2A server to talk to other agents.
A review date and the fallback for people who don't have the API.
Safari's and Firefox's position on the API.
perguntas.explica: A draft can change: revisar_em (YYYY-MM-DD) and fallback. There is no announced stable Chrome date, and browser positions are context (course 2), not a requirement.

itens.texto: Each acronym lives in a layer: discovery, page, server, questions, agents, purchase, identity.
Proposal, draft, project or stable, always with the date you read it.
Adopt, wait or does not apply, with a reason; an adopted draft carries a date and a fallback.
